action_summary: Replaces the hand-written effect list with relations over the machine's own state and measures, on five real machines (filesystem, git, tarball, sqlite, and a sort machine whose only change is the order of lines), what a fixed {CARD, MULTISET} vocabulary cannot state. 3 of 6 requests are unstateable under it and solved under the goal-directed vocabulary, on 3 machines, each decided by the machine's reader and stable on a second read; for 2 of the 3 the atom that solves it is exactly the atom the fixed vocabulary calls inert (mv, sort). 3 atoms invisible to the fixed vocabulary, reproduced by a second full pass. The goal-directed vocabulary uses 3 of 5 relations, so it carries no term a goal does not need. One request is excluded with its measured reason: git identity includes dates, so an amend in the same second is byte-identical. 7.1 s, 0 parameters, 0 model calls, no network.

truth.the_law_this_round_adds: THE VOCABULARY IS THE ARTIFACT. An effect is a computable object -- the set of relations that moved between two readings -- and a goal can only be stated, planned for and verified in relations the system carries. Experience of an atom whose effect no relation names is experience of nothing.
what_is_false_in_the_claim: that experiencing the most advanced action once installs it: mv was experienced in every cell of the probe table twice and still could not take the rename request
that repetition fixes an unstateable goal: a thousand observations of an invisible change are a thousand observations of nothing
that one demonstration identifies the rule: median 1037 surviving programs, 4 of 23 tasks identified
that an action list transfers: 0 of 20 held-out bugs at any budget; an action shape from one demonstration reaches 1-2 of 20
that any of this solves 'any computer use': the five relations are a grammar, not the world, and OSWorld 2.0's hardest phenomena need relations nobody wrote down
